brief: A seed-starting tray of at least four cells, each with a draining bin.

requirements.requirement: Seed-starting tray of at least four cells
requirements.evidence: Four full bases at 0,0 / 1,0 / 0,1 / 1,-1 level 0 form one locked body, each cell holding its own bin; tops view shows 4 seedlings (prop:1-4).

requirements.requirement: Each cell with a draining bin
requirements.evidence: Each of the 4 cells has a hex-bin-full-drain (bin:0,0,0, bin:1,0,0, bin:0,1,0, bin:1,-1,0 ~hex-bin-full-drain).

requirements.requirement: Suitable for seed starting (soil + seedlings shown)
requirements.evidence: fill_and_plant filled all 4 drained bins with soil and planted a seedling in each; check_build clear, no PLANT_NOT_IN_SOIL or prop warnings.

finish.summary: 4-cell seed-starting tray in a 2x2-ish hex cluster: four full bases, each dropped with a full-depth drained bin (hex-bin-full-drain), end-capped and joint-bolted per house rules, then each bin soil-filled and planted. Check_build ok, meshClash clear, ~364x467mm.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.

events.text: Building your 4-cell seed tray — each cell will get its own draining bin for seedlings.
